title: Astra Critical cyber & Law, Claude’s R&D share, Anthropic wet lab, Claude→OpenAI bounty
summary: Five Overheard picks Ed ranked for Sep 19: GPT-6 Astra hits OpenAI Preparedness Critical for cybersecurity (InfoQ); Astra for Law ships with a US legal search index (TNW); Anthropic says Claude now leads about a quarter of its own R&D (Reuters); TechCrunch confirms Anthropic’s Bay Area wet biology lab; Tom’s Hardware covers white-hats using Claude to chain forum/SSO flaws into OpenAI employee ChatGPT/Codex access (bounty paid).

sections.heading: Overheard — picks of the day
bullets: InfoQ (Sep 17): GPT-6 Astra is OpenAI’s first Preparedness “Critical” cybersecurity model — expert-supervised zero-day / exploit-chain evals, with a note that chain-of-thought is harder to monitor than earlier Sol-class models.

The Next Web (Sep 18; launch Sep 17): Astra for Law pairs GPT-6 Astra with a ~230M-URL US legal search index, Trusted Access, and a partner plugin wave (Harvey/Legora building on it). Strong HN discussion the same day.

Reuters (Sep 17): Anthropic says Claude now leads about 26% of internal R&D work building its next models (up from ~1% in March), with wide agent collaboration on research — figures as reported by Reuters from Anthropic.

TechCrunch (Sep 18): Anthropic confirms it operates a Bay Area wet lab that runs physical biology experiments for AI work (not positioned as a drug-discovery shop) — infrastructure signal beside frontier-model pacing debates.

Tom’s Hardware (Sep 18): Hacktron white-hats used Claude Opus 5 (cyber-oriented) to chain a Discourse/libheif RCE with an OpenAI SSO flaw, reaching employee ChatGPT/Codex accounts and proving impact with a harmless internal PR; OpenAI paid a $6,500 bounty after a fast fix.

sections.heading: What this week means for operators
bullets: Astra is no longer just a coding demo — Critical cyber evals plus a vertical Law product show capability and distribution moving together.

Anthropic’s week stacks recursive-internal-use claims (Claude on Claude R&D), physical-world bio tooling, and AI-assisted offensive research that landed inside a peer lab’s employee accounts — all via reputable third-party outlets.
Treat frontier-model helpfulness in security and research workflows as a dual-use control problem: SSO blast radius, forum/image pipelines, agent connectors — not only a model-card footnote.
